notes.calculus-chapter-17-review-1-concept-che: Substitution of e^(rx) yields the characteristic polynomial; each case supplies two independent homogeneous solutions.
notes.calculus-chapter-17-review-4-concept-che: Newton’s law and Kirchhoff’s voltage law lead to the same second-order linear structure, with mass/inductance, damping/resistance and stiffness/inverse capacitance corresponding.
notes.calculus-chapter-17-review-1-true-false-: The homogeneous linear operator applied to a sum is the sum of its zero outputs.
notes.calculus-chapter-17-review-2-true-false-: The operator applied to C₁y₁+C₂y₂ gives (C₁+C₂)x, which equals x only under an additional restriction such as C₁+C₂=1.
notes.calculus-chapter-17-review-3-true-false-: cosh x and sinh x are independent linear combinations of e^x and e^(−x).
notes.calculus-chapter-17-review-4-true-false-: e^x is a homogeneous solution, so the proposed trial gives zero. Resonance requires a trial Ax e^x, with A=1/2.
